A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the GHQ-12, GHQ-30 and GHQ-60 are all good measures of the two most important dimensions of psychological morbidity.
the GHQ is a useful instrument, but that the 12-item version, which has been widely used in epidemiological studies, may be the best choice.
the GHQ-12 is a useful screening instrument for detecting ‘cases’ in a general population, but the GHQ-30 is not.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the GHQ-12, GHQ-30 and GHQ-60 all contain the same two factors: ‘general dysphoria’ and ‘social function/optimisim’.
the factor structure of the General Health questionnaire is stable across different populations and different versions.
